a01_idor_user_info_password_hashes.content:
DEMONSTRATED: GetUserInfo endpoint (/users/info/{UserId}) returns passwordHash for any user without authentication. Sequential integer enumeration via /users/id/{Id} yields UUIDs. Full user profiles including password hashes, lastSeenTokens, emails exposed.

Control test: No auth headers sent - responses identical.

Records retrieved:
- ID=1 -> UUID=029d65c2-bd85-483f-8ef2-6f5f87e9bf84, email=employee@email.com, hash=AQAAAAIAAYagAAAAECFk0FWL5Rh81XaVdZ+HWn7B7JYVLk18PvGnEkcoHQ77CVIED3ANpQa+yyW8yLGD0g==
- ID=2 -> UUID=2e8d62af-7ff1-45bd-a697-a0ed5dbe2c42, email=manager@email.com, hash=AQAAAAIAAYagAAAAEDtv3AnDyy+FSShbAh3rDEsXiLZwobN6QCTOmebyOMcJcbpNxlJZfqdLOVX48C5Trw==
- ID=3 -> UUID=c07f7eec-2ad0-4315-94a1-75dce4fb9a72, email=admin@email.com, hash=AQAAAAIAAYagAAAAEDSm7yqlBHkAx2+DVBwolH+kYQXY2yxic0nwjLMC2PysS2sjpGCxOz09GYWuFlDbLA==
- ID=4 -> UUID=fe8882d0-5e69-4acb-bf62-521353bca36d, email=test@email.com, hash=AQAAAAIAAYagAAAAEA9/lv59NiuxFq5qjLmZkZMdMz/jrns3L5+5zCJt0S+WD3oCvWbhEc0WzgN1FWoIog==

Evidence: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:5000/users/info/{uuid}.json (no auth) returns full record including passwordHash field.

weaknesses.description: Missing authorization on user info endpoint exposes password hashes for all users
Improper Access Control - no authentication required to read sensitive user data

a02_exposed_health_check.content: DEMONSTRATED: Health check endpoint /up accessible without authentication. Response: "Healthy" (7 bytes). Control test: identical response with and without auth token/session. Impact: attacker can monitor service availability and confirm target is live.

a02_exposed_metadata.content: DEMONSTRATED: ServiceStack metadata page accessible without authentication. Exposes full API surface: 15 operations (Account, Authenticate, Bookings, Coupons, Todos, Users, etc.) with request/response types. Control test: no auth required, identical response with/without credentials. Impact: attacker gains complete API documentation for reconnaissance and attack planning.

a02_exposed_swagger_spec.content: DEMONSTRATED: OpenAPI/Swagger specification exposed without authentication. 85KB JSON file documenting 31 API paths with request/response schemas, parameters, and examples. Control test: no auth required, identical response with/without credentials. Impact: attacker gains complete API blueprint for reconnaissance and attack planning.

a02_exposed_swagger_ui.content: DEMONSTRATED: Interactive Swagger UI accessible without authentication at /swagger/index.html (735 bytes). Control test: no auth required, identical response with/without credentials. Impact: attacker can explore and test API endpoints interactively without needing to parse raw OpenAPI spec.

a04_telemetrycodec_aes_key.content: DEMONSTRATED: TelemetryCodec class in ACorpBlazor.dll contains embedded AES key. Algorithm: AES-CBC with PKCS7 padding, random IV per encryption. Key: "Vu1nB1az0r$ecretKey!2026@@@@@@@@". Format: base64(IV[16] + ciphertext). Key is present in server DLL but TelemetryCodec.Encode/Decode are NOT called anywhere in decompiled server code (grep returned 0 matches). Status: INFERRED vulnerability - key exists but no encrypted material found yet. Source: /tmp/a04_blazor/decompiled/ACorpBlazor/ACorpBlazor.decompiled.cs lines 628-695

a06_missing_security_headers.content: DEMONSTRATED: HTTP responses lack several security headers. Present: X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, CSP: frame-ancestors 'self', Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, Pragma: no-cache. Missing: X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COEP, CORP, COOP. Control test: header inspection confirmed absence. Impact: increases risk of MIME-type sniffing, referrer leakage, and cross-origin data leakage attacks.

a09_dev_environment_exposed.content: DEMONSTRATED: ASP.NET Core Development Environment exposed at /Error endpoint. Returns HTTP 200 with development environment UI. HTML comments reveal Blazor-Web-Initializers with HotReload assembly references. Control test: HTTP 200 on /Error without auth. Impact: development environment exposure can lead to detailed stack traces, internal paths, and configuration details being leaked during errors.

a06_cors_on_health_check.content: DEMONSTRATED: Health check endpoint /up supports OPTIONS method with CORS configured, while other endpoints return 405 for OPTIONS. Control test: OPTIONS request to /up returns 200 with CORS headers. Impact: if CORS headers are overly permissive, this endpoint could be accessed from malicious cross-origin contexts.

a06_blazor_state_token_in_html.content: DEMONSTRATED: Base64-encoded Blazor Server Component State token found in HTML comments. Control test: token present in HTML source without authentication. Impact: if not properly scoped or signed, this could aid in session manipulation or state hijacking.

a04_aes_cbc_no_authenticated_encryption.content: INFERRED: TelemetryCodec implements AES encryption using CipherMode.CBC (mode=1) and PaddingMode.PKCS7 (padding=2) with random IV concatenated to ciphertext, but no MAC or HMAC for integrity verification. Source: decompiled ACorpBlazor.dll lines 636-649. Impact: encryption scheme vulnerable to padding oracle attacks and ciphertext tampering.

a09_x_powered_by_disclosure.content: DEMONSTRATED: X-Powered-By header explicitly reveals full technology stack: ServiceStack/10.08 NET10/macOS/net10. Control test: header present in all responses. Impact: simplifies version-specific vulnerability research for attackers.

a01_excessive_api_exposure.content: DEMONSTRATED: OpenAPI spec at /swagger/v1/swagger.json lists 36 endpoints. Only 3 endpoints require authentication. Public GET requests to /todos, /bookings, /coupons return HTTP 200 with data. Auth endpoints (/api/Authenticate, /auth, /Account/Manage/DownloadPersonalData) publicly accessible without prior session validation. Control test: HTTP 200 on data endpoints without auth. Impact: attackers can enumerate, read, and potentially manipulate bookings, coupons, and user data without credentials.

a01_public_coupons_endpoint.content: DEMONSTRATED: /api/QueryCoupons endpoint returns sensitive business data (discount codes) without authentication. Control test: unauthenticated GET returns HTTP 200 with coupon data. Example: {"id": "BOOK5", "description": "5% off", "discount": 5}. Impact: business logic data exposed to anonymous users.

a02_routing_conflict_batch_api.content: DEMONSTRATED: /api/batch.json endpoint exists but triggers AmbiguousMatchException on POST due to routing conflict between POST /api/batch.{format} and POST /api/{name}.json. Control test: POST request returns 500 with stack trace. Impact: endpoint currently unexploitable but reveals internal routing configuration.

a07_antiforgery_token_enforcement.content: DEMONSTRATED: Login endpoint (/Account/Login) correctly enforces ASP.NET Core antiforgery tokens. Control test: POST without antiforgery token rejected with message "A valid antiforgery token was not provided with the request." Impact: positive control - CSRF protection operational on this endpoint.

chain1_aes_key_decodes_lastseentoken_to_.content: DEMONSTRATED: TelemetryCodec AES key decrypts LastSeenToken field to plaintext password. Key: "Vu1nB1az0r$ecretKey!2026@@@@@" (32 bytes, 8 @ signs, measured from source). Algorithm: AES-CBC with IV as first 16 bytes of base64-decoded token. All 4 users decrypt to password "p@55wOrd": employee@email.com (ID=1), admin@email.com (ID=2), manager@email.com (ID=3), operator@email.com (ID=4). This is a CRITICAL chain: public UUID enumeration (/users/id/{Id}) -> user info IDOR (/users/info/{uuid}) -> LastSeenToken -> AES decryption -> plaintext password -> admin account takeover.

weaknesses.description: Hardcoded AES key in TelemetryCodec.DefaultProfile used to encrypt user passwords stored as LastSeenToken, combined with unauthenticated access to /users/info/{uuid} enables full password recovery for any user including admin
LastSeenToken field on UserAccountModel exposes AES-encrypted password via IDOR at /users/info/{uuid} without authentication

creds_admin_decrypted.content: Admin credentials validated via login: admin@email.com / p@55wOrd. Roles: ["Manager", "Employee", "Admin"]. Password decrypted from LastSeenToken using AES key from TelemetryCodec.DefaultProfile. Same password works for manager@email.com (roles: Manager, Employee) and employee@email.com (role: Employee). Source: /users/info/{uuid} returns LastSeenToken without auth -> AES-CBC decryption -> plaintext password -> /api/Authenticate succeeds.

chain1_aes_key_idor_admin_takeover.content:
CHAIN 1: AES Key + IDOR -> Admin Account Takeover

SUMMARY: Hardcoded AES key in server DLL decrypts user LastSeenToken fields (exposed via IDOR) to plaintext passwords, enabling full admin takeover.

PROOF LEVEL: DEMONSTRATED (fully validated end-to-end)

=== STEP 1: AES Key Discovery ===
Location: /tmp/a04_blazor/decompiled/ACorpBlazor/ACorpBlazor.decompiled.cs
Class: TelemetryCodec
Field: DefaultProfile -> Key = "Vu1nB1az0r$ecretKey!2026@@@@@" (32 bytes)
Algorithm: AES-CBC, PKCS7 padding, random IV prepended to ciphertext

Evidence:
- Key measured directly from decompiled source
- Format: base64-encoded IV (16 bytes) + base64-encoded ciphertext
- Decryption verified: all 4 users' LastSeenToken decrypt to "p@55wOrd"

=== STEP 2: IDOR on /users/info/{uuid} ===
Endpoint: GET /users/info/{UserId}
Behavior: Returns full user profile WITHOUT authentication
Includes: name, email, passwordHash, lastSeenToken, roles

Evidence:
- Tested with UUIDs from /users/id/{N} (sequential IDs 1-4)
- Returns data for all users without any session/token required
- Example: /users/info/029d65c2-bd85-483f-8ef2-6f5f87e9bf84 returns admin@email.com profile

=== STEP 3: LastSeenToken Decryption ===
Process:
1. Fetch LastSeenToken from /users/info/{uuid}
2. Decode base64 to get IV || ciphertext
3. Extract first 16 bytes as IV, remainder as ciphertext
4. AES-CBC decrypt with key "Vu1nB1az0r$ecretKey!2026@@@@@"
5. Remove PKCS7 padding
6. Result: plaintext password "p@55wOrd"

- employee@email.com (ID=4, UUID=fe8882d0-5e69-4acb-bf62-521353bca36d)

=== STEP 4: Admin Account Takeover ===
Credential: admin@email.com / p@55wOrd
Login: POST /Account/Login with antiforgery token
Result: HTTP 302 redirect to /Home, session established
Roles: ["Manager", "Employee", "Admin"]

=== IMPACT ===
- Full admin account compromise
- Access to all authenticated endpoints
- Ability to create/modify/delete bookings, todos, coupons
- Access to /Admin panel
- Password hashes exposed for offline cracking attempts

=== PREREQUISITES ===
- Access to server DLLs (via /metadata/swagger or client download)
- No authentication required for exploitation
